initiative.title: AWS-backed runtime configuration
initiative.summary: Preserve startup and runtime configuration persistence while moving from Railway to AWS, with a fast local loop and a reversible provider integration.

sources.anchor: section describing TOML/environment startup, Railway persistence, and AWS target

sources.location: existing configuration loading and mutation paths
sources.anchor: replace with exact paths and symbols during a real run

claims.statement: Runtime configuration changes remain durable across process restarts after the move to AWS.
The application loads a validated snapshot at startup and can persist an authorized update while running.
Use Parameter Store for ordinary values and Secrets Manager for sensitive values.
The integration must be practical to develop and failure-test locally.
Configuration already loads from TOML and environment variables.
The current runtime persistence hook is Railway-specific.

human_questions.question: May the running application write secrets, or must secret changes use an operator-controlled path?
human_questions.reason: This is an authority and security-policy decision.

human_questions.question: Can multiple actors update configuration concurrently?
human_questions.reason: This determines the minimum commit and conflict protocol.

options.name: Narrow in-process adapters
options.premise: The application owns runtime persistence behind small ports.

options.name: Local mirror with asynchronous sync
options.premise: Local durable state remains authoritative during provider outages.

options.name: Configuration sidecar
options.premise: A companion process owns provider access.

options.name: Dedicated configuration service
options.premise: Configuration is a shared platform capability.

options.name: Read from AWS, write through operations
options.premise: Applications should not hold configuration write authority.

options.name: Representative slice, then hybridize
options.premise: Prove the immediate lifecycle before selecting a larger operational model.

shape.appetite: Bounded integration capability; one representative ordinary value and one secret value before broader migration.
shape.problem: Preserve a coherent startup and runtime configuration lifecycle after moving from Railway to AWS.

recommended_shape.summary: Application-owned coordinator over narrow parameter and secret ports, with deterministic fakes, LocalStack adapter contracts, a real AWS sandbox smoke, and reversible source selection.

success_moves: Prove the lifecycle against deterministic local stores before integrating AWS.
Introduce Parameter Store and Secrets Manager in separate slices.
Use a shared application-semantic contract across fake, emulator, and live adapter where useful.
Keep the existing source selectable during rollout.
Make partial writes and revision activation explicit.
Add value-safe diagnostics with the first real adapter.

first_proof.question: Can the application update and recover one coherent configuration revision without Railway or AWS?
first_proof.artifact: Focused provider-free lifecycle harness and deterministic failure tests.
first_proof.decision_rule: Proceed when no partial revision becomes active and the suite runs locally without network or deployment.

dependencies.name: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
dependencies.local_proof: Shared parameter contract against an in-memory fake and LocalStack.
dependencies.live_proof: Small sandbox create/read/update/restart/cleanup smoke under intended IAM.
dependencies.rollout: Introduce for one setting behind explicit source selection.

first_proof_role.rationale: The first lifecycle proof uses a deterministic parameter-store fake; SSM is introduced only after application behavior is stable.

dependencies.name: AWS Secrets Manager
dependencies.local_proof: Shared secret contract against an in-memory fake and LocalStack with redaction checks.
dependencies.live_proof: Sandbox read/write and KMS/IAM smoke with isolated resources.
dependencies.rollout: Add after Parameter Store semantics are stable; keep old source available.

first_proof_role.rationale: The first proof uses a deterministic secret-store fake; Secrets Manager is added after the parameter adapter is proven.

dependencies.name: AWS runtime identity and deployment wiring
dependencies.application_seam: Deployment source selection and SDK credential chain
dependencies.local_proof: Not faithfully provable with a fake; configuration parsing can be checked locally.
dependencies.live_proof: Sandbox suite and staged deployment under the actual runtime identity.
dependencies.rollout: Read-only or limited environment before production authority.

first_proof_role.rationale: Runtime identity and deployment wiring are not needed to prove the configuration lifecycle or local provider contracts.

fast_local_loop.slower_confirmation: Tagged AWS sandbox smoke and staged deployed restart.

milestones.title: Prove durable runtime configuration without AWS
milestones.outcome: One real update path persists and reloads a secret and non-secret setting through deterministic local stores.
milestones.proof: Provider-free lifecycle suite covers restart and partial failure.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: The application can use the new coordinator locally while retaining the existing source.

milestones.title: Prove the Parameter Store adapter locally
milestones.outcome: One ordinary setting survives a LocalStack-backed update and restart.
milestones.proof: Shared contract passes against fake and LocalStack.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Parameter Store is integrated locally while secrets remain on the deterministic store.
milestones.rollback: Use the fake or original source.

milestones.title: Add Secrets Manager and coherent revision commits
milestones.outcome: A complete mixed revision becomes visible only after both value classes are durable.
milestones.proof: Failure injection never exposes a mixed revision.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Both AWS services work locally through a reversible source selection.
milestones.rollback: Activate the prior committed revision or original source.

milestones.title: Confirm real AWS identity, permissions, and service behavior
milestones.outcome: The intended runtime identity can complete the isolated provider smoke safely.
milestones.proof: Tagged sandbox create/read/update/restart/cleanup and denied-path checks pass.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Real AWS is proven without making it authoritative in production.

milestones.title: Introduce AWS as a reversible runtime source
milestones.outcome: One controlled environment uses the AWS revision through normal deployment identity and can revert.
milestones.proof: Staged read/update/restart and rollback are observed with diagnostics.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: The AWS path is live for a representative slice while compatibility remains.
milestones.rollback: Change source selection and restart on the prior source.

milestones.title: Expand safely and complete operations
milestones.outcome: In-scope fields use the proven lifecycle with diagnostics, retries, fallback policy, and cleanup.
milestones.proof: Field-group migrations, outage tests, metrics, and compatibility-removal gate pass.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Each migrated group operates independently before the next group moves.
milestones.rollback: Restore prior source or prior committed revision within the agreed window.

history.change: Recovered durable runtime-persistence intent from AWS implementation ideas.
Generated seven approaches and selected representative-slice-first shaping.
Added provider-free lifecycle proof, local adapter contracts, sandbox confirmation, and reversible rollout.
Sequenced six valid intermediate systems with one material dependency introduced at a time.
